2027-02-19.title: Second Friday of the Great Fast
2027-02-19.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The commandment of God is holy and just
2027-02-19.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). Abstinence from meat; fasting is highly recommended. Way of the Cross.
2027-02-19.verse: Today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt.
theo: The first reading shows us sin from God's side. “The LORD saw that the wickedness of humankind was great in the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of their hearts was only evil continually. And the LORD was sorry that he had made humankind on the earth, and it grieved him to his heart.” We usually think of sin as breaking a rule. Genesis shows it as wounding a heart. The earth “was filled with violence”, and God grieves like a father who watches his children destroy one another. Yet one sentence opens a door: “But Noah found favor in the sight of the LORD.” “Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation; Noah walked with God.” On a Friday of the Great Fast, when we stand before the Cross, we see how far that grief of God went. The heart that was grieved in Genesis is the heart pierced on Calvary.

The second reading is a story of new beginnings at Gilgal. The generation that left Egypt had died in the wilderness, “not having listened to the voice of the LORD.” Their children, born on the journey, are circumcised at Gilgal, and God says: “Today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt.” Then they keep the Passover, and the next day they eat the produce of the land, and “the manna ceased.” The food of the journey gives way to the food of the promised land. During these weeks, and above all around Holy Week, thousands of pilgrims climb the hill of Malayattoor, where tradition remembers St Thomas at prayer. Many go barefoot, some carry wooden crosses, and the slope rings with the old cry, “Ponnin Kurishu Muthappo, ponmala kayattam.” A pilgrimage is a small Gilgal: we carry the disgrace of our old slavery up the hill, and the Lord rolls it away. Paul adds that the law itself was never the problem: “So the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and just and good.” The commandment “You shall not covet” showed Paul his sin, and sin used even the good commandment to deceive him. The law names the illness; only Christ heals it.

In the Gospel the leaders in the temple ask Jesus, “By what authority are you doing these things? Who gave you this authority to do them?” Jesus answers with a question about John's baptism. They calculate: if we say from heaven, he will ask why we did not believe; if we say of human origin, the crowd will turn on us. So they answer: “We do not know.” It is not ignorance; it is refusal. They did know, but they would not say it, because the answer would have asked them to change. Many of our evasions in confession and in prayer sound just like this: I do not know. The Great Fast is the time to stop calculating, to admit what we already know, and to let the Lord roll away our disgrace.
outline: Ask: what does my sin do to the heart of God?
Point 1 · It grieved him to his heart
Sin seen from God's side; Noah who walked with God.
Gilgal, the Passover, and the end of the manna.
It names the illness; Christ heals it.
The evasion that refuses to change.
“Today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt.”
live: Make the Way of the Cross today, at church or at home, and at the twelfth station tell the Lord you are sorry for having grieved his heart.
In your next confession, do not say “I do not know”; name plainly the sin you already know.
Plan a pilgrimage this Lent, to Malayattoor or to a shrine near you, and offer it for someone carrying a disgrace.
2027-02-19.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, our sins grieved the heart of your Father, and on the Cross your own heart was pierced for us. Roll away from us the disgrace of our old slavery, as you did for Israel at Gilgal. Give us the honesty to say what we know, and the courage to change. Feed us on our journey until we reach the land you have promised. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Israel kept the Passover at Gilgal and the manna ceased; in the Holy Qurbana Christ our Passover is offered, and he is the bread for our journey until we eat with him in the kingdom.

quick: Sin grieves the heart of God; the Cross shows how deeply.
At Gilgal God rolled away the disgrace of Egypt; he can roll away ours.
Do not hide behind “we do not know”; say what you know and change.
2027-02-19.action: Make the Way of the Cross today and name one sin plainly before the Lord.
2027-02-19.question: Where am I saying “I do not know” when in fact I know and do not want to change?

family.explain: The Bible says that when people became very wicked, God was sad in his heart. Sin is not just breaking a rule; it makes God sad, the way it makes our parents sad when we hurt each other. But Noah loved God and walked with him, and God was pleased with him. On Fridays of the Great Fast we remember how much Jesus suffered for our sins.
family.intention: We pray for all who suffer because of violence in the world.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do today to make God's heart glad?”

illus: A software engineer from Angamaly, home on leave, climbed the hill of Malayattoor one Lenten night with his father, who insisted on going barefoot. Halfway up the son asked, a little impatiently, why they could not take it easy like the families resting on the rocks. The father said: I am carrying something up this hill that I want to leave there. At the top he went to confession in the queue near the chapel. Coming down at dawn he walked so lightly that the son had to hurry to keep up.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, crucified for us, we gather on this Friday of the fast. Roll away our disgrace and heal us. Amen.
share: It grieved him to his heart (Genesis 6:6). How does it change me to see my sin as grieving God?
Today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt (Joshua 5:9). What disgrace do I want the Lord to roll away?
We do not know (Mark 11:33). Where am I evading a truth I already know?
pm.resp: Lord, by your holy Cross, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the mercy of the Cross.
For places filled with violence, as in the days of Noah.
For pilgrims climbing Malayattoor and all our hill shrines this Lent.
For those who carry a hidden shame and dare not speak of it.
For our group, that we may be honest before God.
pm.close: Father, your heart grieves over our sins, yet you sent your Son to bear them on the Cross. Roll away our disgrace, feed us on our journey, and make us honest and humble before you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Genesis tells us that when the wickedness of humankind became great, the LORD was sorry that he had made humankind, and it grieved him to his heart (Genesis 6:6). Sin is not only breaking a rule. It wounds the heart of God. And on this Friday, before the Cross, we see how far that wound went.
But Noah found favour in the sight of the LORD; he walked with God (Genesis 6:8–9). There is always a door of grace.

At Gilgal God said to his people: today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt (Joshua 5:9). They kept the Passover, and the manna ceased, because they had reached the land. When we go on pilgrimage this Lent, when we go to confession, the Lord rolls away our disgrace too.

In the Gospel the leaders answer Jesus: we do not know (Mark 11:33). They knew, but they did not want to change. Let us not hide behind those words. Let us say honestly what we know, and let the Lord change us. Amen.
kids: Children, the Bible says that sin makes God sad in his heart. Jesus loves us so much that he died on the Cross to take our sins away. Today, let us say sorry to Jesus and make his heart glad.

intro: Theme: “Today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt.”
The grief of God over sin, the new beginning at Gilgal, the holy law, and the evasion that refuses to change.

points.h: It grieved him to his heart
q: And the LORD was sorry that he had made humankind on the earth, and it grieved him to his heart.
And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, with which you were marked with a seal for the day of redemption.
points.apply: Make the Way of the Cross today and offer the Lord your sorrow for having grieved him.

q: The LORD said to Joshua, “Today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt.” And so that place is called Gilgal to this day.
Clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch, as you really are unleavened. For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed.
points.apply: Bring one old disgrace to the Lord in confession this Lent.

q: O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness,
If you continue in my word, you are truly my disciples; and you will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.
points.apply: In your next confession, name plainly what you already know.

concl: Sin grieves the heart of God, and the Cross shows how deeply he loves us still.
Stop calculating; let the Lord roll away your disgrace.
2027-02-19.resolve: Make the Way of the Cross today and go to confession before the end of next week.
